title: Sediment Starvation Below Two Dams: An Illustrative Budget for the Orvine Delta
abstract: Deltas grow only while their rivers deliver more sediment than waves, currents and subsidence remove. Using the Orvine delta, a fictional delta constructed as a worked example, we assemble an illustrative sediment budget for the decades before and after two dams were closed on its main river. In this study's illustrative records, the yearly load arriving at the delta apex declined by roughly 71 percent, and most of the delta front has retreated since 2004. We follow the remaining sediment through the distributary channels, compare the supply with what the delta plain needs to keep its elevation, and discuss which management options could narrow the gap.
